mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 8% triggers a recessionary demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY and UNRATE exceeds 8%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 7% for four consecutive months signals weakening labor demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of four consecutive months with UNRATE above 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing supply, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth above 0.5% monthly for two consecutive months) combined with a concurrent rise in consumer spending (RSAFS growth above 0.4% monthly for two months) signals a robust demand expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly AND RSAFS > 0.4% monthly for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of two consecutive months with PAYEMS > 0.5% and RSAFS > 0.4% growth.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for six consecutive months
regime_hint: prolonged monetary accommodation with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL < 2% for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for five consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of five consecutive months with UNRATE below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 400 thousand units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction-related earnings and broader consumer confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of four consecutive months with HOUST below 400 thousand units.
